text:
Aditya: heads-up — ran a small canary to exercise stale-page reclamation under high-concurrency gen workloads. wanted to share quick findings and ask for design thoughts.
Liz: curious — what trigger did you use and which metric spiked? p99 or p50?
Aditya: triggered by lowering the reclaim window to 60s on a couple canaries. saw overall token throughput unchanged but p99 latency jumped ~18% for short requests. p50 unaffected.
Kevin: 18% p99 is concerning. could be that reclaim is racing with kv-cache warmups. did you see increased page faults / async-migrates?
Aditya: yes, fault rate up ~3x during the window. snippet from the quick log dump:
```
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] reclaim: evicted 8 pages tenant=team-a pod=canary-3
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] async-migrate: queue_len=7 latency_ms=12
[2026-03-18T14:02:12Z] request: id=abc123 seq=1 p99_lat_ms=42
```
Liz: can you share the offload policy? was it aggressive host-staging or full-device evict?
Aditya: host-staging aggressive: we allowed host-backed staging for any page > 4KB if not touched for reclaim_window. no compression.
Kevin: that config explains the p99: short-lived sequences that get their kv cached then have it evicted and must rehydrate on next token. reclaim should prefer cold prefix pages (long-unused) not recently active kv entries.
Liz: agree. maybe we need two-tier eviction hints: "soft reclaim" for true cold pages and "hard reclaim" only when memory pressure is sustained.
kevin: also worth considering an API surface: allocation-level hint flag `reclaim_hint=IMMORTAL|COLD|PREFER_STAGING`. that avoids evicting pinned-ish allocations like recent kv caches.
Aditya: love the hint idea. for the experiment i can flip to soft reclaim (mark pages reclaimable but keep them in host warm pool for N seconds) and rerun. would that be acceptable as a short-term mitigation?
Liz: yeah, short-term mitigation + telemetry. we need to capture: per-tenant fault rate, kv-cache-hit-after-evict, token-latency-delta, and async-migrate queue depth.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout for reclaim-experiment started (canary-3, canary-5) — 2 hosts.
Aditya: thanks. i'll add telemetry dashboards and run soft-reclaim for 6 hours. will post results.
Kevin: long-term: propose RFC followup to add reclaim_hint to allocator API and define semantics for soft vs hard reclaim and migration priority. also include test harness to simulate rapid anti-locality (e.g., many short chats interleaved).
Liz: and add an experiment plan that varies reclaim_window, staging-warm-pool-ttl, and compression-on-evict. attribute impact to each axis.
Aditya: action items: 1) run soft-reclaim canary (me) 2) add telemetry panels (me + liz) 3) draft RFC sketch for reclaim_hint (kevin) 4) define perf test scenarios (liz). i'll update here with a follow-up thread later today. :thumbsup:
Liz: thanks — ping me if you need help instrumenting the kv-cache metrics.
Kevin: i'll start a skeleton RFC doc and link here.
Aditya: end-of-thread note: early takeaway — reclaim aggressiveness needs workload-aware heuristics; blanket time-based eviction hurts short-lived kv locality.
